problems.quote: limiting the tenure of the Governor‑General to five years
problems.problem: The Regulating Act 1773 did not fix a five‑year term; the Governor‑General held office at the pleasure of the Crown.
problems.correction: leaving the Governor‑General’s tenure at the Crown’s pleasure
problems.verifierReason: Regulating Act 1773 did not fix a term; Governor-General served at Crown's pleasure. Correction accurate.

problems.quote: policy errors — such as the mismanagement of the Bengal famine of 1770 — could not be easily corrected
problems.problem: The Bengal famine of 1770 occurred before the Regulating Act (1773); the Act was not responsible for its mismanagement.
problems.correction: policy errors — such as the mismanagement of the Bengal famine of 1770 — were not addressed by the Act
problems.verifierReason: Famine of 1770 predated Regulating Act 1773; Act did not address it. Correction accurate.

problems.quote: creating a reservoir of discontent that would later feed into the larger uprising of 1857
problems.problem: The Forest Acts of 1865 and 1878 were enacted after the 1857 Revolt, so they could not have contributed to discontent leading to 1857.
problems.correction: creating a reservoir of discontent that fueled later tribal uprisings
problems.verifierReason: Forest Acts 1865/1878 postdated 1857 revolt; they fueled later tribal uprisings, not 1857. Correction accurate.

problems.quote: the arrival of the “Army of the Punjab” under Sir Colin Campbell, the decisive victory at the Siege of Delhi in September 1857
problems.problem: Sir Colin Campbell commanded the relief of Lucknow, not the Siege of Delhi; the Delhi siege was led by the Punjab Movable Column under John Nicholson.
problems.correction: the arrival of the Punjab Movable Column under John Nicholson, the decisive victory at the Siege of Delhi in September 1857
problems.verifierReason: Sir Colin Campbell commanded Lucknow relief, not Delhi siege; Delhi led by Nicholson's Punjab Movable Column. Correction accurate.

problems.quote: allowing payloads of up to ten tonnes to be delivered to geostationary transfer orbit
problems.problem: GSLV Mk III (LVM3) can deliver up to 4 tonnes to GTO, not 10 tonnes
problems.correction: allowing payloads of up to four tonnes to be delivered to geostationary transfer orbit
problems.verifierReason: LVM3 GTO capacity is ~4 tonnes, not 10 tonnes; correction is accurate.

problems.quote: The Indian National Committee for Space Research has sponsored the development of Hall‑effect thrusters and gridded ion engines
problems.problem: Indian National Committee for Space Research (INCOSPAR) was dissolved in 1969; current sponsor is ISRO/Department of Space
problems.correction: ISRO has sponsored the development of Hall‑effect thrusters and gridded ion engines
problems.verifierReason: INCOSPAR dissolved in 1969; ISRO is the current sponsor; correction is accurate.

problems.quote: participation in the International Lunar Research Station led by China and Russia
problems.problem: India is not a participant in the China-Russia led International Lunar Research Station
problems.correction: independent lunar exploration initiatives
problems.verifierReason: India is not part of the China-Russia ILRS; it pursues independent lunar missions; correction is accurate.

problems.quote: integrated electric propulsion
problems.problem: INS Vikrant uses COGAG gas turbine propulsion, not integrated electric propulsion
problems.correction: conventional gas turbine propulsion
problems.verifierReason: INS Vikrant uses COGAG gas turbines, not integrated electric propulsion; correction is accurate.

problems.quote: combat management system developed by the Naval Physical and Oceanographic Laboratory
problems.problem: Combat management system for Vikrant is developed by Bharat Electronics Limited, not NPOL
problems.correction: combat management system developed by Bharat Electronics Limited
problems.verifierReason: Combat Management System for Vikrant is developed by BEL, not NPOL; correction is accurate.

problems.quote: culminating in the nuclear‑powered ballistic missile submarine (SSBN) Arihant class that completes the nuclear triad
problems.problem: Project 75/75I are conventional submarine programmes; Arihant class SSBN is a separate programme
problems.correction: while the nuclear‑powered ballistic missile submarine (SSBN) Arihant class completes the nuclear triad
problems.verifierReason: Arihant SSBN is a separate programme from Project 75/75I; 'culminating in' wrongly links them; correction properly separates the fact.

problems.quote: incorporates cross‑border transfer mechanisms (adequacy decisions, standard contractual clauses) compatible with DFFT
problems.problem: The Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 does not contain adequacy decisions or standard contractual clauses; it empowers the central government to notify countries to which transfers are allowed.
problems.correction: provides for cross‑border transfers via government notification of permitted countries, compatible with DFFT
problems.verifierReason: DPDP Act 2023 uses notification-based regime, not adequacy/SCCs; correction accurately reflects this.

problems.quote: India participates in the Multi‑Party Interim Appeal Arbitration Arrangement (MPIA) to preserve binding appeal rights
problems.problem: India is not a participant in the MPIA; it has not joined the arrangement.
problems.correction: India has not joined the Multi‑Party Interim Appeal Arbitration Arrangement (MPIA)
problems.verifierReason: India has not joined MPIA; correction states this fact correctly.

problems.quote: He studied at the Jesuit college in Paris
problems.problem: Diderot studied at the Jesuit college in Langres, not Paris
problems.correction: He studied at the Jesuit college in Langres
problems.verifierReason: Diderot studied at the Jesuit college in Langres, not Paris; correction is accurate.

problems.quote: Diderot completed the remaining 17 years of work alone
problems.problem: From 1758 to 1772 is 14 years, not 17
problems.correction: Diderot completed the remaining 14 years of work alone
problems.verifierReason: 1758 to 1772 is 14 years, not 17; correction fixes the arithmetic error.

problems.quote: D'Alembert resigned as co-editor in 1758 after the Encyclopédie was formally banned
problems.problem: The Encyclopédie was formally banned in 1759, after D'Alembert's resignation
problems.correction: D'Alembert resigned as co-editor in 1758 before the Encyclopédie was formally banned
problems.verifierReason: D'Alembert resigned in 1758; the formal ban came in 1759; correction correctly reverses the sequence.

problems.quote: free trade benefits all nations through comparative advantage and the enlargement of markets
problems.problem: Comparative advantage was developed by David Ricardo, not Adam Smith; Smith argued for absolute advantage
problems.correction: free trade benefits all nations through absolute advantage and the enlargement of markets
problems.verifierReason: Smith advocated absolute advantage; comparative advantage is Ricardo's; correction substitutes the correct concept.

problems.quote: The earliest panels, associated with microlithic assemblages, suggest a broad bracket of roughly 30,000–10,000 BP
problems.problem: Microlithic assemblages in South Asia are characteristic of the Mesolithic (c. 10,000–5,000 BP), not the Upper Palaeolithic. The earliest Bhimbetka panels (Upper Palaeolithic) are associated with blade and burin industries, not microliths.
problems.correction: The earliest panels, associated with Upper Palaeolithic blade industries, suggest a broad bracket of roughly 30,000–10,000 BP
problems.verifierReason: Original incorrectly links earliest Bhimbetka art to microliths (Mesolithic); correction accurately assigns Upper Palaeolithic blade/burin industries.

problems.quote: 2022 Punjab floods, 2023 Marathwada drought same year
problems.problem: The two events occurred in different years (2022 and 2023), so they are not in the same year.
problems.correction: 2022 Punjab floods and 2023 Marathwada drought
problems.verifierReason: Original claims two events in different years are 'same year' - clearly false; correction removes contradiction accurately.

problems.quote: NCRB: 10,881 farmer suicides 2022
problems.problem: NCRB data records 10,881 farmer suicides in 2021; the 2022 figure is 11,290.
problems.correction: NCRB: 11,290 farmer suicides 2022
problems.verifierReason: 10,881 is 2021 figure; 11,290 is correct 2022 NCRB farmer suicide count - correction is accurate.

problems.problem: No such laser cleaning trials at Akbar's Tomb have been formally incorporated into ASI's standard operating procedure; laser cleaning remains experimental and is not standard practice for Mughal painted plaster conservation in India.
problems.correction: Laser cleaning trials at the Tomb of Akbar (Sikandra, 1613 CE) demonstrated that a 1064 nm Nd:YAG laser at 0.5 J/cm² removes soot without ablating the underlying pigment, a finding that informs conser
problems.verifierReason: ASI has not adopted laser cleaning as SOP for Mughal painted plaster; it remains experimental. Correction accurately states trials inform research.

problems.quote: later Gupta rulers such as Kumāragupta I and Skandagupta
problems.problem: Kumāragupta I (c. 415–455 CE) and Skandagupta (c. 455–467 CE) are mid‑5th‑century rulers, not “later Gupta rulers” of the early 6th century when the Parvati Temple was built.
problems.correction: later Gupta rulers such as Budhagupta
problems.verifierReason: Kumaragupta I and Skandagupta are mid‑5th century, not early‑6th; Budhagupta correctly represents a later Gupta ruler.

problems.quote: a coin of Rudradāman I reads “Rajno Mahakṣatrapasa Rudradamasa” with the year 150 (228 CE)
problems.problem: Rudradāman I’s coins bear dates around Saka year 72 (150 CE); year 150 (228 CE) belongs to a much later Kṣatrapa ruler.
problems.correction: a coin of Rudradāman I reads “Rajno Mahakṣatrapasa Rudradamasa” with the year 72 (150 CE)
problems.verifierReason: Rudradaman I's coins are dated Saka 72 (~150 CE); year 150 (228 CE) belongs to a later ruler.

problems.quote: karshapana weight ≈ 11 g
problems.problem: The karshapana is a weight standard of approximately 3.4 g (for silver); Satavahana lead coins weigh around 11 g but are not described as ‘karshapana weight’.
problems.correction: lead coins of about 11 g
problems.verifierReason: Karshapana weight standard is ~3.4g silver; 11g refers to Satavahana lead coins, not the standard.

problems.quote: Other notable contributors to the revival include T. Balasaraswati, who maintained the traditional Sadir aesthetic and emotional depth, and the Tanjore Quartet (Chinnayya, Ponniah, Sivanandam, and Vad
problems.problem: The Tanjore Quartet (early 19th century) systematized the original Sadir/Bharatanatyam repertoire; they were not contributors to the 1930s revival.
problems.correction: Other notable contributors to the revival include T. Balasaraswati, who maintained the traditional Sadir aesthetic and emotional depth. The Tanjore Quartet (Chinnayya, Ponniah, Sivanandam, and Vadivel
problems.verifierReason: Tanjore Quartet (early 1800s) systematized Sadir repertoire; they predate 1930s revival. Correction accurately separates their earlier role from revival contributors.

problems.quote: Britain's population rose from 6.5 million in 1750 to 16.8 million in 1850
problems.problem: The figures 6.5 million (1750) and 16.8 million (1850) refer to England and Wales, not Great Britain (which included Scotland). Great Britain's population was about 7.5 million in 1750 and 21 million in 1850.
problems.correction: England and Wales' population rose from 6.5 million in 1750 to 16.8 million in 1850
problems.verifierReason: Original mislabels England+Wales figures as Britain; correction accurately limits to England and Wales.

problems.quote: France's Melin tariff 1892
problems.problem: Misspelling of the French tariff name; it was the Méline tariff (named after Jules Méline).
problems.correction: France's Méline tariff 1892
problems.verifierReason: Original misspells 'Méline'; correction fixes spelling accurately.

problems.quote: attended by 14 European powers plus the USA and the Ottoman Empire
problems.problem: The Berlin Conference had 14 participating nations in total, including the USA and the Ottoman Empire, not 14 European powers plus those two.
problems.correction: attended by 14 powers including the USA and the Ottoman Empire
problems.verifierReason: Berlin Conference had 14 total participants, not 14 European plus two; correction accurate.

problems.quote: The Treaty of Portsmouth (1905) gave Japan control of the Liaodong Peninsula
problems.problem: The treaty granted Japan the South Manchurian Railway and the lease of Port Arthur, but not sovereignty over the Liaodong Peninsula.
problems.correction: The Treaty of Portsmouth (1905) gave Japan the South Manchurian Railway and the lease of Port Arthur
problems.verifierReason: Original incorrectly states Japan got control of entire Liaodong Peninsula; treaty only gave lease of Port Arthur and railway rights.

problems.quote: freed 48 million serfs
problems.problem: The emancipation freed about 23 million serfs, not 48 million.
problems.correction: freed roughly 23 million serfs
problems.verifierReason: Original figure 48 million is wrong; emancipation freed about 23 million serfs.

problems.quote: The Battle of Berlin (April-May 1945) — 1M Soviet casualties
problems.problem: The figure of 1 million Soviet casualties for the Battle of Berlin is a significant overestimate; Soviet archival data puts total casualties (killed, wounded, missing) at approximately 350,000.
problems.correction: The Battle of Berlin (April-May 1945) — ~350,000 Soviet casualties
problems.verifierReason: Soviet archival data (Krivosheev) confirms ~361k total casualties; 1M is a gross overestimate.

problems.quote: Bretton Woods (1944) created the IMF, the World Bank, and GATT
problems.problem: The Bretton Woods Conference (1944) established the IMF and the World Bank; GATT was negotiated separately in 1947 and was not a product of Bretton Woods.
problems.correction: Bretton Woods (1944) created the IMF and the World Bank; GATT was negotiated in 1947
problems.verifierReason: Bretton Woods created only IMF and World Bank; GATT was negotiated separately in 1947.
